responsibilities: Work closely with relevant business functions to understand business domains, processes, and data structures.
Contribute to solutions related to data migration, data modeling, data validation, and data governance.
Coordinate with stakeholders to understand data requirements, including user insights, customer journeys, and business metrics.
Translate business requirements into meaningful data implementations, analyses, datasets, reports, and dashboards using BI tools.
Analyze data to identify trends, patterns, and actionable insights that support strategic business planning.
Collaborate with Data Engineers to develop efficient frameworks and tools for data quality and data lineage.
Coach and support business users in understanding and effectively using BI reports and dashboards.
Perform data audits and root-cause analysis to identify and resolve data mismatches across systems when needed.

evidence.velocity_vs_rigour: Collaborate with Data Engineers to develop efficient frameworks and tools for data quality and data lineage.
evidence.velocity_vs_rigour_explanation: Rigour: validation, governance, lineage and 'data audits and root-cause analysis' run through the responsibilities, and the only speed phrase ('fast-growing environment') sits in the benefits section.
evidence.domain_risk: Be part of a mission-driven fintech company transforming financial access for millions of underserved Vietnamese workers.
evidence.domain_risk_explanation: High: this is consumer lending — a fintech serving millions of workers, with 'Intelligent Credit Scoring implementation' named among the preferred skills.
evidence.data_team_maturity: Collaborate with Data Engineers to develop efficient frameworks and tools for data quality and data lineage.
evidence.data_team_maturity_explanation: Mid: separate Data Engineer and junior Data Analyst cohorts already exist and BI tooling is deployed, but the JD still describes data migration and governance work in progress.
evidence.jd_authorship: Coordinate with stakeholders to understand data requirements, including user insights, customer journeys, and business metrics.
evidence.jd_authorship_explanation: Mixed: bullets like data audits and lineage frameworks are concrete, while others — 'Coordinate with stakeholders to understand data requirements' — would fit any data role.
evidence.stakeholder_orientation: Coach and support business users in understanding and effectively using BI reports and dashboards.
evidence.stakeholder_orientation_explanation: Mixed: half the bullets serve unnamed business users through BI, and the other half serve the data function itself — modelling, governance, lineage and mentoring analysts — with neither dominant.
evidence.autonomy_level: Contribute to solutions related to data migration, data modeling, data validation, and data governance.
evidence.autonomy_level_explanation: Execution: the verbs are 'Contribute to', 'Coordinate', 'Collaborate', 'Translate' and 'Support', with no bullet giving the role ownership of direction.
evidence.ai_role: Experience using AI-assisted tools to automate data workflows and support complex data architecture and modeling.
evidence.ai_role_explanation: Ai_user: the candidate is asked to use AI tools to speed up their own data work, not to build anything AI consumes.
evidence.testing_framing: Collaborate with Data Engineers to develop efficient frameworks and tools for data quality and data lineage.
evidence.testing_framing_explanation: Responsibility: building data quality and lineage frameworks is a responsibility bullet, not a tool named in the skills list.
evidence.loss_aversion_framing: Perform data audits and root-cause analysis to identify and resolve data mismatches across systems when needed.
evidence.loss_aversion_framing_explanation: Moderate: the fear is data mismatches between systems and is handled operationally, with no compliance or regulatory language despite the fintech setting.
evidence.greenfield_vs_fix: Contribute to solutions related to data migration, data modeling, data validation, and data governance.
evidence.greenfield_vs_fix_explanation: Fix_scale: the infrastructure work is migration plus resolving 'data mismatches across systems', not building something new.
evidence.loss_aversion: Risk is framed as inconsistent numbers between systems: 'Perform data audits and root-cause analysis to identify and resolve data mismatches across systems when needed.'
